To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
endothelin (ET) is reduced in the kidney transplant during vascular rejection, and that the ET content in the kidney is reduced in chronic CyA toxicity.
endothelin immunostainings are reduced in intrarenal vessels in vascular rejection, but are normal in other forms of renal transplant rejection.

the immunostaining of endothelial cells for ET is decreased in kidney transplant biopsied with signs of endothelial rejection and that the presence of chronic Cy A toxicity is associated with a reduction of intrarrenal ET immunostaining.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunostainability of ET in kidney transplant biopsied and in normal kidneys.
the pathophysiological role of ET in the renal transplant.
the role of endothelin (ET) in kidney transplant pathology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
endothelial damage leads to a decrease in intrarenal ET immunostaining and this is not only the case in vascular rejection but also in other forms of endothelial damage, like ATN or CyA toxicity.
the ET system is involved in the pathogenesis of ATN, acute vascular rejection and CyA toxicity.
the immunostaining pattern in kidney transplant biopsied depends on the type of rejection and on the presence of chronic Cy A toxicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ET plays an important role in the pathophysiology of kidney transplantation.
ET is not only a marker for endothelial damage but also an important mediator of endothelial dysfunction.
ET is an important vasoactive peptide in kidney transplantation and that its local production and action in the transplanted kidney is altered by various pathophysiologic processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
endothelial damage in the kidney transplant can lead to a decrease in intrarenal endothelin levels.
the endothelium is the primary target for endothelin in the kidney.
ET is a marker for endothelial damage and that it can be used in the differential diagnosis of renal transplant rejection.
